basis: D5: the firm's own page describes a seed-stage vehicle founded by NEA and anchored at Harvard SEAS that invests in startups; a fund-shaped entry, not an operating company.

D5 and D1: the page is NEA's stake in IndoUS Ventures, the 2006-07 India joint venture fund with IndoUS Venture Partners (later Kalaari Capital); the firm's own page calls it an India-focused venture fund.

D5: the firm's own page describes a medical device incubator; ExploraMed entities form and spin out device companies (Acclarent, NeoTract and Moximed are their own rows), so the page is program-shaped. Flagged for review.

X1 (T3): Info Edge (Naukri) listed in India in 2006, before NEA's India team existed; the firm's own 2014-15 page labels it growth and IPO/Public, and no NEA private round before the listing is on record, so the position is a listed purchase.

The firm's 2014-15 page lists Future Retail (India's listed retailer, the former Pantaloon Retail) as private, stage early; the company was listed long before 2014, so the position is either an X1 listed purchase or a stake in an unlisted Future Group entity. No source found resolves which.

R1 control addendum: Everside Health is Paladina Health renamed (November 2020); on 2018-06-01 NEA funds acquired, through NEAPH Holdings, all of the outstanding equity of Paladina from DaVita for about $60M in cash (Everside's 2021 draft S-1, Certain Relationships; Healthcare Dive, 2018-06-07). A control purchase, not a venture round. Same company as the row paladina-health.

note: Captora, adaptive marketing software. The firm's 2014 year matches its $22M second round (May 2014, Marketing Dive), which followed a Series A, but no page read names NEA in it, hence low confidence. State unknown, aligned with the Bain Capital Ventures book (San Mateo).
CareWise, Seattle, healthcare demand management; the firm's historical list gives the exit as acquired by PhyCor. No round naming NEA was found.

CCP Games (EVE Online), Reykjavik. NEA first invested in 2015 (the firm's 2026 post) in an 18-year-old studio majority-held by Novator and General Catalyst, so the entry is Growth. Pearl Abyss bought CCP in 2018; on 2026-05-01 it was sold back to its management for $120M and renamed Fenris Creations (Wikipedia), with NEA backing it again. Private, fresher than the a16z book's acquired. Same company as the row fenris-creations.
CellGate, polyamine-analogue cancer drugs; the firm's historical list gives the exit as acquired by Progen Pharmaceuticals (Australia). No round naming NEA was found.

Chinaway (Huitong Tianxia) is the Beijing logistics IoT company that trades as G7 (identification from knowledge; the firm's description matches). G7 raised $200M led by Trustbridge at about a $2.2B valuation in February 2022 (Caixin Global), stale. The round NEA entered by 2013 is not on record.
Choosy, New York social-media-driven fashion; the firm's archived page labels the 2018 investment Seed. Defunct, aligned with the Coatue book. Graduation left for the graduation pass.
Cirtas Systems, San Jose, cloud storage controllers; it pulled its product and wound down around 2011 to 2012 (from knowledge). No round naming NEA was found.
CITIC Pharmaceuticals, China-based pharmaceutical distribution; the firm's own 2013 and 2015 releases say it was acquired by Shanghai Pharmaceuticals. No round naming NEA was found.

Console, an interconnection platform founded in 2011; in October 2017 PCCW Global took its brand, platform and team (Console Connect) and IX Reach its network business (Capacity Media), so acquired. Not the Thrive book's Console (AI IT support, San Francisco): a name collision. Its city and the round NEA entered are not on record.
Convex Computer, Richardson, Texas, minisupercomputers; bought by Hewlett-Packard in 1995 (Wikipedia). The 1980s round NEA entered is not on record.

CoreStory, San Francisco, AI code intelligence for legacy modernization. NEA co-led the $32M Series A (SiliconANGLE, 2025-10-28), but the firm gives 2022 as its first year, so the entry is an earlier, undisclosed round: undetermined. Momentum check 2026-09-30: no round at $1B or more reported; the Series A is the last priced round, below $1B.

funding_rounds.lead: Tribeca Venture Partners, NEA, SineWave Ventures

note: Corvita, Miami, small-diameter synthetic vascular grafts; the firm's historical list gives the exit as acquired by Pfizer. No round naming NEA was found.
CruiseWise, online cruise booking; the firm's archived page labels the 2011 investment seed and gives the exit as acquired by TripAdvisor. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Data-Tamer was the early name of Tamr (Cambridge, Massachusetts; Stonebraker and Palmer), the same company as the row tamr. The firm's archived page labels the 2013 investment seed; the $18M Series B1 of 2018 (Boston Business Journal) is a named later round and graduates the row.

Drive.ai, Mountain View self-driving software; NEA led its $50M Series B in June 2017, its first round (the early $12M came from Northern Light, Oriza and InnoSpring). Apple bought the company in June 2019 days before it would have shut down (The Verge).

Elance, freelance services marketplace; merged with oDesk in December 2013 as Elance-oDesk, renamed Upwork in 2015 (Wikipedia). Under D8 Elance is the member and the Upwork row is not. The round NEA entered in 2003 is not on record.

EnVerv, smart-grid communications system-on-chip; the firm's own page gives the exit as acquired by Semtech, fresher than the Benchmark book's unknown. Its city and the round NEA entered are not on record.
Fantasy Shopper Limited, an Exeter social shopping game; members' voluntary liquidation from 2014-03-26, dissolved 2015-04-07 (Companies House, liquidators in Exeter). No round naming NEA was found.

Feather, New York furniture rental; the firm's archived page labels the 2017 investment seed. Spark led its $12M Series A in May 2019 (AlleyWatch), which graduates the row; Vesta bought Feather and Fernish in November 2023 (Business of Home).

Fetchr, Dubai delivery; NEA led its $11M Series A in 2015 and the $41M Series B in 2017 (MENAbytes); a $1.3M seed came first without NEA named. The firm's 2014 year is read as the close year. Its top backer warned of liquidation in October 2021 (Bloomberg); no later outcome was found. Not the Y Combinator book's Fetchr (San Francisco): a probable name collision.
ForHealth Technologies, Daytona Beach, IV drug preparation automation; the firm's historical list gives the exit as acquired by Baxa. No round naming NEA was found.

GaoV appears only as a name on the firm's 2008 China portfolio page, with no description. Google News finds no matching company (Gtel results are a Zimbabwe phone brand), so the company cannot be identified.

Gtel appears only as a name on the firm's 2008 China portfolio page, with no description. Google News finds no matching company (Gtel results are a Zimbabwe phone brand), so the company cannot be identified.

Hello Alfred (now Alfred), New York; Wikipedia names NEA in the April 2015 $10.5M Series A and not in the November 2014 seed (Spark, SV Angel, CrunchFund), so the entry is the Series A. Same company as the row alfred, aligned with it and with the Spark book.
Hospital Group of America, a chain of free-standing psychiatric hospitals on the firm's 2008 historical list; its fate, city and the round NEA entered could not be established.
Hospital Partners of America, Charlotte, developer of physician-partnered acute care hospitals; current on the firm's 2008 list, later fate not established.
Huddler, a SaaS platform for enthusiast discussion forums, first invested 2009; Google News carries nothing on it, and its fate, city and round could not be established.
IBAH, Blue Bell, Pennsylvania, contract clinical research; acquired by Omnicare in 1998 (from knowledge). The round NEA entered is not on record.

Imergy Power Systems (formerly Deeya Energy, the row deeya-energy-inc), Fremont, vanadium flow batteries; it entered insolvency and laid off its staff in August 2016 (Energy-Storage.News). The round NEA entered in 2007 is not on record.
inTarvo, Indian technical support and reverse logistics for electronics OEMs; the firm's archived page labels the 2009 investment growth. Its later state could not be established.

Konarka, Lowell, Massachusetts, organic photovoltaics; NEA was among its venture investors by 2006, but no round is named. It filed Chapter 7 in May 2012, ceased operations and was liquidated (Wikipedia).
Koozoo, crowd-sourced live video of public places from smartphones, on the firm's 2013 list only; Google News has nothing on it, and its fate, city and round could not be established.
KOR Electronics, Cypress, California, DRFM and electronic warfare systems; acquired by Mercury Computer Systems in 2011, as the firm's historical list says. No round naming NEA was found.

Leyden Energy, Fremont, lithium-ion batteries. In June 2014 A123 Systems bought certain intellectual property and technical staff (Windpower Engineering), not the company or its business, which ended; so defunct under the acqui-hire rule, aligned with the Lightspeed book, although the firm's exit line reads acquired by A123.
LifeMetrix, cancer treatment programs and information services, on the firm's historical list; its fate, city and round could not be established.
Likelihood, real-time retail customer-intent prediction, first invested 2012; Google News returns only the common word, and its fate, city and round could not be established.
Lot18, New York online wine retailer; NEA led its $10M Series B in May 2011 after FirstMark's Series A. It laid off staff and closed in 2023 (Wikipedia).
LSF Network, performance-based online advertising and lead generation, first invested 2004; its fate, city and round could not be established.
Lytmus, virtual-machine job try-outs for digital skills, San Francisco; aligned with the a16z book (unknown). Not the 2026 Indian edtech Lytmus AI. The round NEA entered is not on record.
